taxonomyNote: NatureServe lists the extant species as Kinosternon stejnegeri (McCord 2016; TTWG 2025), restricting the name K. arizonense to fossil material; it was formerly treated as a subspecies of K. flavescens.
fieldMarks: Dome-shaped carapace that lacks keels, brown, olive or yellow-brown; plastron and marginal rim yellow.
Top of head grey; underside and sides of head cream to light yellow.
behavior: Active by day, and also at night in the July-August monsoon; spends most of that period in water.
Hibernates in a burrow in winter; in drought can stay dormant underground for up to two years.
Eats frogs, tadpoles, toads, fish, aquatic invertebrates and carrion.
habitat: Prefers temporary ponds and puddles; found in Sonoran desert scrub and semidesert grassland.
range: Arizona in the United States (NatureServe lists AZ only) and Sonora, Mexico.
